conviction_note: Ten small, mostly offsetting findings sum to +0.4. The CFO's 17-Sep primary transcript (services 20%+, removed-but-not-inducted engines +60% YoY, CFM56 retirements 1.5%, 2027 colour promised 'in October') argues against the Melius 'high-single-digit 2027 aftermarket' call that drove the 19% de-rating. Against it: full-year EPS consensus already sits above the $7.85 guide top, global RPK went flat-to-negative in Jul-Aug while GE had assumed modest H2 departure growth, and the stock sold its last three beat-and-raises by 4-7%. So p_up is 51, abs_move is 6.0 (implied 5.82, median reaction 5.56, plus a likely 2027 framework), and the scaled number is +0.12. The findings sum and the scaled number agree in sign; the scaled number is smaller because the reaction function on this name has vetoed good prints three times running.

findings.finding: At Morgan Stanley Laguna on 2026-09-17, GE's CFO Rahul Ghai gave forward numbers that cut against the 2027 aftermarket bear case. He said CES services will grow 20%+ in 2026 (guide: low 20s). Engines removed but not inducted are up ~60% YoY. CFM56 retirements are tracking 1.5-2% (closer to 1.5%), against the 3-4% the company originally assumed and the 3-4% its own internal 2027/28 numbers were built on. Fleet-wide retirements are down ~10% YoY. CFM56 shop visits are 'closer to 2,400 than 2,300' for 2026 and 2027. Engine removals are expected up >10% in 1H27, so 2027 services growth could exceed the double-digit algorithm. GEnx deliveries are growing faster in Q3 than Q2's +50%. He said 'things look as good as they possibly can' and promised 2027 colour 'as we get into October'. The market expectation sits on Melius's 09-14 call that aftermarket growth slows to high single digits in 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three prints raised or reaffirmed guidance on strong services and fell: 2026-07-16 -4.06 (beat and raise), 2026-04-21 -5.56 (beat, guide held toward the high end), 2026-01-22 -7.38. The prior raise on 2025-10-21 rose +1.31; on 2025-04-22 and 2025-01-23 the stock rose 6-7% on guidance. Good services numbers have not been paid while the stock sat near highs. Now it is 18% off the high.
findings.why_not_priced: The transcript is public, but the stock still fell to a closing-basis drawdown of -19.5% on 09-15 and sits ~18% off its high. Ghai spoke two days after the Melius downgrade and the stock did not recover: $317.89 on 09-29, $312 now. The tape is pricing the 'aftermarket peak in 2027' narrative, not the company's removal and induction data. If the market had priced Ghai's 2027 removal and retirement numbers, the stock would have re-rated toward the ~$390 consensus target and the 20-day run-up would be positive rather than -2.2%. The 2027 framework itself is not public until the call.
findings.independence: AAR (2026-09-28, separate finding) said it was 'not seeing a slowdown anywhere in our bookings in parts'. Bernstein's 10-15/18 note calls the aftermarket robust (https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9129034/ge-aerospace-ge-maintains-strong-growth-outlook-despite-fuel-price-concerns). TIKR's 2026-09-30 summary of the same transcript (https://www.tikr.com/blog/ge-aerospace-stock-is-17-below-its-high-heres-what-its-cfm56-retirement-data-means-for-2027) is the same document, not independent.

findings.finding: The bar is above the guide. 247wallst puts FY2026 adj EPS consensus at $7.92, above the $7.85 top of the July guide. Benzinga's quarterly consensus (Q3 $1.99 + Q4 $2.20 = $4.19 for H2) sits above the H2 the guide implies: $7.65-7.85 less H1 actuals of $1.86 + $2.02 = $3.77-3.97. H1 operating profit was $5.3B, and the $10.55-10.75B guide implies H2 of $5.25-5.45B, flat on H1 despite a 'bigger, better second half'. So a raise to roughly $7.95-8.05 is needed just to meet the Street, and a raise only to the top of the old range would disappoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In July GE raised EPS guide midpoint by $0.50 to $7.65-7.85 (consensus had been $7.54) and the stock still fell 4.06%. In April 2026 it held guide 'trending to the high end' and the stock fell 5.56%. Raises that merely meet a raised Street have been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the Street's own expectation, so it is priced as a level. What is not priced is the asymmetry: the derated stock may be pricing a raise, so a raise that only reaches consensus pays nothing. The skew is only +1.64, so the options market is not paying up for a guide disappointment.
findings.independence: Benzinga quarterly estimates (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/GE/earnings-forecasts) give Q3 $1.99 and Q4 $2.20, i.e. ~$8.07 for the year by arithmetic. The guide is from the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000040545/000004054526000047/ge2q2026earningsrelease.htm) and H1 operating profit from Leeham (https://leehamnews.com/2026/07/16/q2-2026-earnings-ge-aerospace-keeps-the-beat-despite-a-few-missed-notes/). The FY consensus is single-sourced, so the size is capped.

findings.finding: Global air traffic went flat-to-negative in Q3. IATA RPKs were +0.2% YoY in July and -0.8% in August, with the Middle East -14.6% and ex-Middle East only +0.6%. GE had said in July that it expected departures to return to 'modest growth' in H2 after a roughly flat H1. Airlines are cutting: Delta's Q3 (10-09) showed flat capacity and fuel expense +62%, United took 5 points of capacity out and flagged further Q4 cuts, and Gulf Coast jet fuel peaked at $4.705/gal in mid-September, the highest since 2022. The risk is softer spare-parts orders or commentary. GE said in July that spare-parts orders were 'normalizing from a very high level' and that delinquencies rose 20% sequentially.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In April 2026 GE cut its departures outlook to flat/low-single-digit on the Iran conflict and the stock fell 5.56% despite a beat. The July print, which flagged flat H1 departures and supply-constrained spares, fell 4.06%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Ghai acknowledged on 09-17 that 'traffic growth has been slow the last couple of months', and the 19% drawdown carries the fuel and traffic story. What remains unpriced is the gap between GE's own H2 departure assumption and a negative August, which could reach Q3 spare-parts orders or the 2027 framing. If the market had fully priced a Q3 spares slowdown, consensus Q3 revenue growth (+12-14%) would have been cut; Yahoo says estimates were reaffirmed over the last 30 days.
findings.independence: Proxy, not a company number. GE's July departures commentary: https://leehamnews.com/2026/07/16/q2-2026-earnings-ge-aerospace-keeps-the-beat-despite-a-few-missed-notes/. Delta Q3: https://beancount.io/pt/blog/2026/10/10/delta-air-lines-q3-2026-earnings-analysis. Jet fuel: https://www.globalair.com/articles/aviation-fuel-spotlight-oil-is-flowing-but-jet-a-didnt-get-the-memo/12728. Counter-evidence: GE says 95% of Q3 spare-parts revenue was in backlog entering the quarter, and the 09-17 transcript says removed-but-not-inducted engines are +60%.

findings.finding: AAR, an aftermarket counterparty, reported on 2026-09-28, after GE last spoke, for the quarter to 2026-08-31. New-parts Distribution grew 23% organically and total sales grew 24% (11% organic). AAR raised its FY27 guide to low-teens growth, and the CEO said 'we are not seeing a slowdown anywhere in our bookings in parts' and that customers do not expect a maintenance slowdown, despite fuel.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Aftermarket strength was the core of every recent GE beat. It was paid in Jan-Apr 2025 (+6.6, +6.07) and not paid in 2026 (-7.38, -5.56, -4.06).
findings.why_not_priced: AAR's quarter overlaps two-thirds of GE's Q3 and contradicts the fuel-driven 'airlines defer maintenance' worry, yet GE traded down from $317.89 on 09-29 to $312 now. If the read-through were priced, GE's Q3 services estimates would have risen; Yahoo reports them only 'reaffirmed'.
findings.independence: AAR 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000001750/000110465926111403/tm2626100d2_ex99-1.htm). This is a proxy, since AAR's distribution mix is not GE parts. It is directionally consistent with GE's own 09-17 removal data, a separate document.

findings.finding: HEICO's Flight Support Group, a direct aftermarket peer, grew organic net sales 12% in its fiscal Q3 to 2026-07-31. That is below its 15% nine-month organic rate, a sequential deceleration in aftermarket parts demand that overlaps July, the first month of GE's Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same aftermarket line as the AAR finding.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. Melius downgraded HEICO with GE on 09-14 on an aftermarket slowdown thesis. It is filed because it is one of the few hard numbers on Q3-period aftermarket demand. It would be unpriced only if GE's Q3 services growth were modelled flat on Q2's +26%.
findings.independence: Points the opposite way from AAR (filed above). Melius downgrade covering both names: https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/5-aviation-stocks-slide-melius-warns-years-of-robust-aftermarket-growth-ending/cZtmcbvRBRF

findings.finding: Q3 airframe deliveries were flat YoY, so LEAP OE volume is likely flat on Q3 2025's 511 engines. Boeing delivered 161 jets in Q3 (124 737s) against 160 a year earlier. Airbus delivered 196 (67 Jul + 57 Aug + 72 Sep) against roughly 201. This sits inside GE's guide: H1 LEAP +41% against a full-year 'high teens' implies a roughly flat H2. Lower OE growth than H1 also eases the mix drag behind Q2's 160bp CES margin decline (installed-engine growth), a modest margin positive. Ghai said GEnx OE deliveries would grow faster than Q2's +50% in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July print fell 4.06% partly on 'civil-engine supply constraints limiting near-term upside' and a 130bp total margin decline. OE volume against margin has been a talking point on each 2026 print.
findings.why_not_priced: Delivery counts are public. The margin read-through (fewer loss-making OE engines means better CES margin than Q2's 27.3%) is inference and not in any preview found. Previews flag only the 'tough LEAP comp'.
findings.independence: Airbus September deliveries: https://www.airdatanews.com/airbus-delivers-72-jets-in-september-as-order-backlog-falls-by-58-aircraft/. Airbus July: https://aircargoweek.com/airbus-reports-204-new-orders-and-67-aircraft-deliveries-in-july/. GE margin attribution: Q2 8-K. This is inference for the margin part.

findings.finding: IEEPA tariff refunds are probably still landing. GE's Q2 10-Q says it filed refund requests and received a portion of previously paid IEEPA tariffs in Q2 (Leeham puts it at ~$100M). CBP Phase 2 refund processing began 2026-06-29 with 60-90 days to issue, so further refunds plausibly landed in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 refund came with a beat that fell 4.06%; it was not paid.
findings.why_not_priced: It may help the EPS beat by a few cents, but on a $2.00 quarter it has no path to the multiple. It is sized as a one-off.
findings.independence: Leeham, $100M refund in Q2: https://leehamnews.com/2026/07/16/q2-2026-earnings-ge-aerospace-keeps-the-beat-despite-a-few-missed-notes/. EisnerAmper on CBP timing: https://www.eisneramper.com/insights/manufacturing-distribution/ieepa-tariff-refunds-accounting-considerations-0826/

findings.finding: On 2026-09-08 GE agreed to buy Consolidated Precision Products for $11.75B, ~$7B in cash and the rest in new debt, closing in 2H 2027. GE says it is EPS and FCF accretive in year one and that capital-allocation plans are unchanged. Commentators cite it as a reason for the de-rating (leverage, regulatory risk), and the call will be the first earnings-call Q&A on it, including the buyback pace.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print with an acquisition of this size as a standalone company.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced; it was announced six weeks ago. The question it raises is answered: the money buys castings capacity for a supply-constrained ramp (Ghai on 09-17: material receipts up nine straight quarters, 'hard capacity' needed), so it is not distress. Near zero; slightly negative only if the call trims the 2026 buyback.
findings.independence: Optionbeast (2026-10-17) names CPP as one of two reasons for the drawdown: https://wp.optionbeast.com/2026/10/17/ge-aerospace-is-19-off-its-peak-monday-will-say-why/

findings.finding: Two program frictions may draw call questions. GE9X: the new mid-seal began shipping to Boeing in Q3 with FAA certification of the part expected 'in the next few months', the existing mid-seal is used for ETOPS certification, and GE9X program losses are guided to rise through ~2028. MAX 10: the FAA delayed certification on 2026-09-28, and GE fell 2.7% that day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GE fell 2.7% on the 09-28 MAX 10 news (TIKR). There is no print reaction history on GE9X.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and known. A charge or retrofit cost for the GE9X mid-seal in the Q3 numbers would be new; none has been disclosed.
findings.independence: MAX 10 delay: https://www.tikr.com/blog/ge-aerospace-stock-is-17-below-its-high-heres-what-its-cfm56-retirement-data-means-for-2027. This shares the Laguna transcript with finding 1.

findings.why_not_priced: The skew is only +1.64 and the implied move of 5.82 is close to the median reaction, so options price neither a squeeze nor capitulation. This is a lean, not a fact about the print.

findings.finding: CFM signed an MoU with Turkish Airlines on 2026-10-16 for 300+ LEAP-1B engines including spares, plus a services agreement covering 600+ engines across Turkish and AJet. This adds to Ghai's 09-17 tally of ~1,800 Farnborough engine orders, IndiGo's 1,000+ LEAP-1A and a 100-engine Korean Air order. These are Q4 orders, so they reach the print only through commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 orders +87% and Q2 +17% were not paid (the stock fell both times).
findings.why_not_priced: Order headlines are public and this stock does not trade on orders. Sized at zero.

outside_window.finding: RTX (Pratt & Whitney) reports Q3 on 2026-10-21, and Safran's Q3 revenue (LEAP deliveries, spares) comes later in October. Both are read-throughs on CFM and the aftermarket that land after GE's reaction session.

Ghai expects FAA certification of the GE9X new mid-seal 'in the next few months'. The LEAP-1B durability kit enters the fleet in Q1 2027, and the CPP acquisition closes in 2H 2027 pending regulatory approval.

baseline_tension: The evidence is balanced, like the skew (+1.64, 'balanced'). The company's own primary data leans mildly positive against a de-rated, short-covered tape. The FY consensus above the guide and the flat-to-negative August traffic lean negative, so nothing found cuts hard against the option market.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the 09-17 CFO transcript finding cut from +1.5 to +1.0, because this name sold its last three beat-and-raises; p_up 52 -> 51.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the FY-consensus-above-guide finding cut from -1.0 to -0.7, because the FY figure ($7.92) has one source plus my own arithmetic from Benzinga's quarterly numbers.

Lesson 5 (proxy vs company number): IATA departures cut from -0.8 to -0.5, AAR from +0.5 to +0.4 and HEICO from -0.3 to -0.2. All are proxies, and GE's own 09-17 document addresses the traffic softness directly.
Lesson 2 (one-offs): the IEEPA tariff refund cut from +0.2 to +0.1, since it has no path to the guide or the multiple.

Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest checked (1.1% of float, DTC 2.4, falling), so no negative needed shrinking for a crowded short; the positioning lean cut from +0.5 to +0.3 as colour rather than evidence.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): CPP kept near zero after confirming the money buys castings capacity for a supply-constrained ramp.
